::: {.why}
The gap you found last night does not shrink, which means a stochastic integral is not defined until you say where in each interval you evaluate, and the financial reason for choosing the left is worth more than the mathematical one.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Say why the left-endpoint convention is the one that makes financial sense, in terms of what a trader knows when.
- State the Itô isometry and use it to compute the variance of a simple stochastic integral.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Read the construction of the Itô integral in the CMU or Etheridge notes, as far as the isometry. The construction is from simple predictable integrands, which is exactly a trading strategy that holds a fixed position between rebalances, and that correspondence is worth making explicit as you read.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Make the financial argument in writing: the left-endpoint convention means your position over an interval is decided before the interval's price change is known. Any other convention lets the strategy see the increment it is about to profit from, which is the look-ahead you spent phase 5 eliminating, in continuous time.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Use the isometry once: compute the variance of the integral of a deterministic function against Brownian motion, and check it by simulation.
:::
:::
